documents.title: Sealed Dispatch, Corridor Line Office
documents.found: In the marshal's pouch, sealed. Pritchard breaks the seal and reads it out at the hand-off; afterwards it lies on his desk
documents.text:
CORRIDOR LINE OFFICE, IRON JUNCTION
BY HAND OF MARSHAL T. GANTT
TO THE SHERIFF AT MERCY CROSSING. NO OTHER.

Owen,

Three things in one month.

Greenwater's winter grain was loaded and did not arrive.
Red Hollow has chained its own mine and will not say why.
Rails are being lifted in Sawtooth Cut. Four trains so far.

I do not believe in three accidents. Somebody is being paid,
and paid in coin I have not seen before.

I have a name. I will not put it on paper. I will say it to
you across your own desk with the door shut.

If I do not come, I was right.

Hold this. Trust nobody who offers to help you carry it.

T. G.

documents.title: The Stranger and the Tellico Road
documents.found: Sold by Tolly Granger at the town gate for a penny once the first chapter is complete. Printed hearsay, not a record. This sheet is sold when the recorded Chapter 1 outcome is saved
documents.text:
THE STRANGER AND THE TELLICO ROAD
A new ballad. T. Granger, printer. One penny.
Set from accounts heard in Mercy Crossing.

Come gather, valley people, where the road comes down the grade;
I'll sell the news I've gathered, and the rhymes that I have made.
A train came off at Tellico. A stranger reached our town.
The rest depends on who you ask, and what they won't set down.

One tells it over supper; one swears the telling's wrong.
I've ink enough for either, but there's only room for song.
I did not ride that morning or stand beside the load.
I set what folk have told me of the strangers on the road.

The word came down that trouble met an unexpected hand.
What happened past the telling wasn't mine to understand.
No singer owns the reason, and no verse can set the fee:
Ask those who came to Mercy what that mercy ought to be.

I set what folk have told me of the strangers on the road.

News came down to Mercy with a space beside the rein.
They argued who had seen the road, then argued it again.
What passed between the strangers is a thing I did not see.
I set the tale upon the sheet; the judgement isn't free.

The quiet after trading had a name that wasn't there.
You ask me who was paid for it; I only sell the sheet.
To call it trade is easy from a dry and distant seat.

documents.title: Rules of the Yard
documents.found: Painted on a boiler plate bolted to the gate at Iron Junction
documents.text:
IRON JUNCTION
A. LOCKRIDGE, YARDMASTER

1. This is a railway. Everything else is somebody's opinion.
2. Arms are worn outside the gate or handed to the gateman.
   The gateman has a list. Do not be on it.
3. No car leaves this yard that has not been passed and
   stamped by the Inspector of Way.
4. No man, woman or child rides for nothing. Brahmin by weight.
5. The yardmaster's office turns to face trouble.
   If it is facing you, consider your position.
6. Trains leave on time. If you are not aboard,
   that was your decision.

documents.title: Chalk on a Boiler
documents.found: Chalked in a careful hand on the boiler of each of the four wrecks along the line; the number is different on each
documents.text:
No. 212

There is power in the blood.

Gauge at point of failure: 4 ft 9 3/4 in.
Passed as sound, stamped, on the 3rd inst.
Who signed?

documents.title: Reward: The Preacher Dole
documents.found: Pasted up at Iron Junction, at the gap, and on the notice board at Mercy Crossing
documents.text:
REWARD
FIVE HUNDRED CAPS

For the person, living, of the train-wrecker calling himself
PREACHER DOLE
of the gang known as the Black Rail.

Tall. Grey. Frock coat and a railwayman's cap. Carries a hymnal
on a chain and wears an inspector's brass gauge at the neck.
Will speak pleasantly. Do not let him finish.

Two hundred caps dead, if it cannot be helped.

The Corridor line pays on delivery to the yardmaster,
Iron Junction. No questions will be asked of the bearer
that the bearer does not care to answer.

documents.title: Flyleaf of a Hymnal
documents.found: Inside the front board of the hymnal chained to Dole's belt
documents.text:
This book the property of
R. OSTRANDER
Inspector of Way, Corridor Line
Iron Junction

Presented by the yardmaster and hands
on the completion of ten years' service.
May he find us always in good order.

(below, in pencil, in another hand)

Reuben. You were right about the trestle.
I ran it anyway. A.

documents.title: The Queen of Tellico: Handbill
documents.found: Nailed to every piling at Greenwater landing, and floating in the lake
documents.text:
TONIGHT AND EVERY NIGHT
aboard the palatial sternwheeler
QUEEN OF TELLICO
Commodore L. Hatcher, Prop.

FARO. MONTE. THE WHEEL.
Music by the Lake Orchestra.

NEW THIS SEASON: play for CORN.
Finest valley meal, by the cup, at the high table.
Why queue for a ladle when you may WIN A SACK?

Skiffs leave the steeple on the hour.
Gentlemen will check their arms. Ladies need not.

The management regrets that it cannot extend credit
to residents of Greenwater.

documents.title: Ration Board, Greenwater
documents.found: Chalked on a slate on the cook-shed door; the figures have been rubbed out and lowered several times
documents.text:
GREENWATER STORES
O. Starnes keeps the count.

Meal in the bin:        9 days
Days to the dogwood:    90
Grown:                  1 cup, morning
Under twelve:           1 cup, morning. 1/2 cup, night
Nursing:                as under twelve, and ask
Sick:                   ask

Nobody is fed twice. Nobody is fed first.
If you think the count is wrong, come and count it.

The grain barge is not lost.
Everybody can see where it is.

documents.title: A Letter of Hire
documents.found: In the strongbox under the faro table on the Queen of Tellico, wrapped round a roll of silver
documents.text:
Commodore,

Enclosed, forty. Count them.

You will take the Greenwater barge under tow on the night of
the new moon and hold it at your anchorage. You will say it
was adrift. You will hold it until first frost and then let it
be found.

You are not asked to sink it, sell it or open a sack.
You are asked for a delay.

Forty more on release.

Do not write back. Do not ask the bearer who sends this.
The bearer does not know.

(no signature. Pressed into the wax, a small plain square.)

documents.title: Tolls at the Gap
documents.found: On a board beside the log barrier where the pike crosses the gap
documents.text:
BY ORDER OF THE DOMINION
Col. A. Brigg, commanding

THIS ROAD IS KEPT. THE KEEPING IS PAID FOR.

Person on foot                      2 caps
Person with pack                    3 caps
Pack brahmin, the head              4 caps
Wagon, the wheel                    3 caps
Drove stock, the score              10 caps
Arms carried openly                 no charge. Recorded
Arms carried otherwise              forfeit

Road-agents taken on the pike are tried at this gate.
Court sits at noon.
The beam is inspected weekly.

documents.title: Docket of the Circuit
documents.found: Pinned to the tailboard of Judge Quill's wagon
documents.text:
CIRCUIT COURT OF THE DOMINION
The Hon. E. Quill

TODAY

1. The Dominion against a road-agent of the Tellico Cutters.
   Robbery upon the highway. Plea: not asked.
   Sentence at noon.

2. Applications for mercy will be heard from persons able
   to state them in complete sentences.

3. Fines are payable to the clerk. Receipts are given.
   The court does not make change.

Persons interfering with the rope will be charged for the rope.

documents.title: Chalk on a Shovel Blade
documents.found: On a shovel sent up in the cage from the Nine level, the night before the Mouth was chained. Blevins keeps it under his cot with the lamp
documents.text:
WE ARE 11. ALL LIVING.
AIR BAD AT THE FACE. WATER TO THE KNEE.
BROKE THROUGH AT THE END OF 9.
IT IS NOT ROCK BEHIND. IT IS A ROOM.
SOMEBODY CUT IT.

WE KNOCKED FOR YOU.
SOMETHING KNOCKED BACK
AND IT WAS NOT YOU.

SEND THE CAGE.
PELL

documents.title: Decoration Day at the Camp-Ground
documents.found: On the notice board at Mercy Crossing and on every gatepost in the valleys, in the week before the fair
documents.text:
DECORATION DAY
at the old camp-ground, Mercy Crossing

Graves dressed from sunup. Bring flowers. Paper will do.
Singing at ten. Dinner on the ground at noon.
Bring a dish and take one home.

BEEF SHOOT at two. Four caps the share.
One ball, sixty paces. Miss A. Pike judges.

FIDDLERS' CONTEST after.

By particular request of the Sheriff, there will attend,
to say their piece and hear ours:
The Compact. The Commonwealth. The Dominion. The Directorate.

NO GUN HAS BEEN DRAWN ON THIS GROUND
ON DECORATION DAY IN FORTY YEARS.
O. Pritchard asks that you remember it.

documents.title: An Empty Cartridge Case
documents.found: Standing on end on the bell-rail of the meeting shed roof
documents.text:
A pistol case, spent. Longer than any pistol round sold in the valleys.

Not brass. Silver, or near it, and turned on a lathe by somebody patient.

No maker's mark. Where one would be, the metal has been filed bright.

It was not dropped. It was stood on end, square to the rail, to be found.

documents.title: What Was in the Courier's Case
documents.found: In the tin map case chained to the courier's wrist
documents.text:
A strip of thin brass, a hand long, punched with rows of small
round holes. No two rows alike.

A sketch in pencil: a long ridge, a notch in it, and under the
notch eleven small lamps drawn in a line where no town is.
Beside it: BLACKSTONE. COUNTED THEM THREE NIGHTS RUNNING.

A slip of ledger paper, torn from a larger sheet. One line:

    4117    quiet, 4 heads, the month    pd.

The hand is small, upright and very neat.
Anybody who has ever had credit in Mercy Crossing knows it.

documents.title: A Page of the Black Book
documents.found: The book in the safe in Vane's counting room. Page 4117 is the last one written
documents.text:
4117

RAIL    Cut, Sawtooth. By E.D.                 30   pd.
RIVER   Barge held, Greenwater. By L.H.        40   pd.
        NOTE: L.H. has not released. Not paid the second 40.
MINE    Mouth kept shut. By H.B.               25   pd.
ROAD    Tellico. Four hands, to wait. By R.D.  20   pd.
        NOTE: R.D. exceeded. A wagon. I did not ask for a wagon.

Paid out, the month                           115

RECEIVED, by the night freight                150
        from  [a small square, drawn in ink]

Balance to the school roof, the clinic stove,
and a widow's account, which I have marked paid.

Six years. No garrison. No list. No gate.
I should like it noted that it worked.

documents.title: Last Testament of S. Vane
documents.found: In the safe, under the black book
documents.text:
I, Silas Vane, merchant, of Mercy Crossing, being of sound mind
and entirely aware of what is likely to become of me:

To Temperance Beckett, the trading post, its stock and its good
will, such as remains. She will run it better than I have.
She is to burn the second book unread. She will not.

To Owen Pritchard, my chess set, and my apology,
which he will understand in time and not accept.

To the town of Mercy Crossing, every debt owing to me, cancelled.

To myself, nothing. I have had my share.

I do not know who sent the silver. I thought it better not to.
That is the only cowardice I will own to.

S. V.

documents.title: A Weight Sheet
documents.found: Folded into the lining of the receiving book at the freight desk
documents.text:
Weighed by me, alone, after hours. C. Haskell.

Crate, sealed, consigned S. Vane.
Off the night freight, from beyond Iron Junction.
Waybill gives origin as BLACKSTONE STA.

Entered on the waybill as: dry goods, 11 lb.
On my scale:               91 lb.

I weighed it three times.

I have not opened it. I have not said anything.
I have written it down. That is what I do.
